jobs.title: The whole country feeds him
jobs.subject: In a Vietnamese communal courtyard, villagers gather food to support Thánh Gióng and the country's defense. Gióng, an ordinary adult in a red tunic, stands among them at the same eye level and body scale. He helps by carrying one ordinary rice sack against his waist with both hands supporting its weight. Beside him at the same depth is a farmer carrying two balanced rice baskets on a shoulder pole; a woman carries a modest sealed fish-sauce jar supported by both hands; a hill villager carries bamboo shoots in a back basket. A few villagers queue through the gate behind them. Thánh Gióng participates in their work with a grateful, determined expression; he does not tower above them or touch a roof. On clean woven mats in the foreground are exactly SEVEN shallow trays of rice, clearly arranged as four in one row and three in another, and exactly THREE separate trays of aubergines in a third row. These are shared provisions, kept away from people's feet. The communal hall and gate are spacious, with lintels well above every adult's head. No worship or ceremonial elevation of the hero.

jobs.title: The iron horse is forged
jobs.subject: A village workshop prepares equipment for the country's defense. Three ordinary adults of the same body and head scale cooperate: a smith holds a heated iron plate with long tongs on a secure anvil and raises a hammer in the other hand; a second smith works bellows connected to a small brick forge; Thánh Gióng, fully dressed in his ordinary red tunic and indigo trousers, stands at the same depth beside them holding a cooled plain blunt-ended iron staff with both hands and helping inspect their work. Gióng is no taller or broader than the other men. Nearby is a normal adult-horse-sized iron horse being assembled from dark hammered plates with sparse rivets and believable four-legged construction; its withers are near an adult man's upper chest, and its feet rest firmly on the ground. Show a finished solid torso and a small loose plate on a workbench, not an open vessel or a casting cavity. A plain adult-sized iron cuirass with shoulder straps rests on a separate stable wooden rack; this is the armor Gióng will wear in battle. The hot forge is separated from the horse and woodwork. No molten metal pouring, no pouring into a finished horse, no unsupported glowing liquid, no bare hands touching hot iron, no giant observer, no oversized horse or equipment.

jobs.title: He rides
jobs.subject: Thánh Gióng, an ordinary-sized Vietnamese young adult with exceptional strength, rides a normal adult-horse-sized iron horse into a scattering invading force. His head, torso, arms and legs are the SAME scale as the nearby adult soldiers; he is elevated only because he is seated in the saddle. He wears the plain dark iron cuirass made in the workshop over his red tunic, with indigo trousers and a simple red headband. He sits astride with a balanced riding posture, visible near leg bent down beside the saddle, his left hand holding the reins. His right hand firmly wraps the bare lower culm of ONE mostly straight uprooted bamboo stalk, very close to its root end. Only a short basal stub about one hand-length protrudes below the fist, with small roots at that end; the long continuous shaft extends diagonally up and forward toward the enemy, with a compact leafy crown only at its far upper end. His four fingers and thumb close around the main stalk with a natural wrist angle. He never grips a side branch, the middle of the plant, leafy tips or root hairs. Several clearly separated broken pieces of his iron staff lie on a clear patch of ground behind the horse. The iron horse has dark hammered metal plates, sparse rivets, four coherent legs, and solid hooves; its hind hooves support a modest rear, and a compact stylized flame emerges from its mouth into empty space ahead. Two ordinary-sized enemy soldiers retreat to the right, one carrying a banner and another carrying a shield; show coherent running poses with no piled or tangled bodies and no gore. Both faces have natural human features in restrained folk-print style, turned right toward their escape direction, with heads seated naturally on their necks. Use clear profiles or gentle three-quarter views, correctly placed eyes, nose, mouth, jaw and ear, and tense but restrained expressions. Avoid twisted necks, grotesque grimaces, bulging eyes, stretched mouths and goofy grins. A few villagers watch from behind a distant protective dyke. The action should read as a human defender using extraordinary strength and forged equipment, not a deity, giant, flying warrior or invulnerable god.

jobs.title: Sóc Sơn
jobs.subject: After defending the country, an ordinary Vietnamese young adult Thánh Gióng leaves quietly along a solid mountain path at Sóc Sơn. He walks on the ground in his simple red tunic, indigo trousers and cloth headband, leading the same normal adult-horse-sized iron horse by a loosely held rein attached to its bridle; both man and horse have visible feet or hooves contacting the path in coherent walking poses. The horse has the same dark hammered plates and sparse rivets as the forge and battle scenes; its withers are near the man's upper chest. His plain iron cuirass from the battle lies with its straps resting naturally on a flat stone beside the path; no ornate plumed helmet. Small ordinary hoofprints hold a little rainwater behind them; farther down the slope, separate small natural ponds and a bamboo grove colored warm ochre suggest the landscape's memory. Keep natural body and object scales. The hero does not fly, ascend, glow, receive worship or ride on clouds. A few curled folk cloud motifs may decorate the open sky but are separate from the figures and never support them. Peaceful, humble departure with human dignity.
